entries.summary: Meditation can rot or rust objects and kill mundane things in an area, and weapon strikes gain greatly increased Attack and Penetration; the magus can no longer enter Final Twilight.
quotes: They have four times the usual Attack Total, and can injure creatures immune to non-magical attacks.
This power's Penetration is (magus's Enigmatic Wisdom x 5), taking the Form of the weapon's striking edge.
which can be no wider than 500 feet across per level of Enigmatic Wisdom that the magus possesses

entries.title: Station That Repels and Attracts Elements
entries.summary: The magus can attract or repel objects of a single Form at will, limited by combined weight, with no Penetration and no effect on warded objects.
quotes: provided their combined weight does not exceed the magus's weight multiplied by three

entries.title: Station That Charms the Elements
entries.summary: The magus can talk to elementally pure objects and persuade their spirits to give information or move, using Presence + Charm rolls against Ease Factors set by the request.
quotes: With a Presence + Charm roll against an Ease Factor of 9 a magus can convince a spirit to give information, or to move in minor, useful ways.

entries.title: Station of Golden Cider
entries.summary: The magus strips supernatural properties from items, creatures and some Gifts by touch after a preparatory meditation, at the cost of losing Creo with most Forms.
quotes: the magus must have an Enigmatic Wisdom score at least one-fifth of the victim's Magic Resistance
this power has a Penetration score of (Enigmatic Wisdom x 5), with a Form of Corpus

entries.title: Repose on the Path of Strife
entries.summary: Followers of this path cannot enter Final Twilight and instead die creating adulterations, so many end their lives by using Golden Cider on themselves.

entries.title: Path of Walking Backwards
entries.requires: House Criamon: Path of Walking Backwards
entries.summary: Introduces the Path of Walking Backwards and lets followers choose a reasoned labyrinth walk or an ecstatic dance; dancers use Dexterity for Enigmatic Wisdom rolls during labyrinth meditations.
quotes: Spinners and dancers use Dexterity rather than Intelligence when making Enigmatic Wisdom rolls during Labyrinth meditations

entries.title: Station of Service to Harmony
entries.requires: House Criamon: Path of Walking Backwards
entries.summary: First station: after purification under a Mystagogue the magus's Gift becomes Gentle, or a Blatant Gift is removed.
quotes: The Gift of most characters on this path becomes Gentle.

entries.title: Station of Rice and Honey
entries.requires: House Criamon: Path of Walking Backwards
entries.summary: By labyrinth meditation the magus restores damaged objects to wholeness and can hold a dying person on the threshold of death for a limited time, but gains the Noncombatant Flaw.
quotes: This power has a Penetration score of the magus's Enigmatic Wisdom multiplied by five.
A magus may safely continue performing meditations for a number of hours equal to his Enigmatic Wisdom score.

entries.title: Station of Expression
entries.requires: House Criamon: Path of Walking Backwards
entries.summary: The magus gains Free Expression and Inspirational, may use Enigmatic Wisdom as an artistic skill, and can convey complex ideas through artworks to mundane audiences.
quotes: Each magus who completes this avenue gains the Virtues Free Expression and Inspirational, and may use Enigmatic Wisdom in lieu of one artistic skill

entries.title: Station of Exaltation
entries.requires: House Criamon: Path of Walking Backwards
entries.summary: By labyrinth meditation the magus draws out a latent positive property from a mundane object, with a difficult roll needed to know which will appear; the magus loses Perdo with most Forms.
quotes: an extremely difficult Intelligence + Enigmatic Wisdom roll (Ease Factor 21 or more)

entries.title: Threshold of Repose on the Path of Walking Backwards
entries.requires: House Criamon: Path of Walking Backwards
entries.summary: The final station lets the magus freely change age, gender and species and choose the time of death, or ascend to join the Spharios.
quotes: A magus of this station may select his age, gender, and species as often as he wishes, taking only the time of a breath to change.

entries.title: Twilight and Walking Backwards
entries.requires: House Criamon: Path of Walking Backwards
entries.summary: The threshold of repose gives no Twilight immunity, though abstaining from magic and strong supernatural auras and avoiding multiple Warping Points at once avoids Twilight.
quotes: magi who abstain from all use of magic and stay out of powerful supernatural auras can avoid entering Twilight by avoiding gaining two or more Warping Points at once

entries.title: Criamon Player Characters in the End of Time
entries.requires: House Criamon player characters in the End of Time chapter
entries.summary: Guidance for involving Criamon player magi in the doomsday plot: how much they learn as their understanding grows, what tasks the House asks of them (vis tribute, research resources, helping Andreva, preparing the move to Megiddo), and how secret to keep it.
quotes: Those recently out of apprenticeship are considered young and unreliable

entries.title: Divine and Infernal Player Characters in the End of Time
entries.requires: Characters with Divine or Infernal patrons
entries.summary: Notes that characters with Divine or Infernal patrons may receive visions or premonitions about each event, which should point toward House Criamon, even though the potential end of time is not God's will.
quotes: Any Divine or Infernal visions or premonitions concerning story events should point the character squarely at House Criamon.

entries.title: Everything is a Lie: What Criamon Know of the Plan
entries.requires: House Criamon, Enigmatic Wisdom or House Criamon Lore
entries.summary: A table of how much a Criamon knows of the plot to end time according to their Enigmatic Wisdom or House Criamon Lore score, plus the note that once the breakthrough is made Criamon magi can be initiated into the new mysteries at Enigmatic Wisdom 7.
quotes: magi of House Criamon are offered initiation into the secret new mysteries of the House when they reach Enigmatic Wisdom level 7
The world will escape all time with the coming conjunction on December 23rd in the year 1277.

entries.title: Bjornaer: The Heartbeast
entries.requires: House Bjornaer: Initiation into the Heartbeast mystery
entries.summary: Bjornaer magi take the form of one mundane creature using the Heartbeast Ability; the form cannot be changed by Hermetic magic, they can cast in beast form at a penalty, cannot bind familiars, and gain little Warping from changing.
quotes: In that case, a roll of Stamina + Heartbeast against an Ease Factor set by the storyguide allows the character to change anyway.
As a rule of thumb, 3 + the magnitude of the transforming magic is a reasonable number.

entries.title: Clan Arelie (Bjornaer clan and initiations)
entries.summary: Describes the Remember clan, its political stance and roles, and lists its three Clan Initiations (the Trial of the Tree, the Deed of Forgotten Lore and the Oath of the Empty Hand) with the Virtues and Flaws each grants.
quotes: The initiate is hanged by his wrists for four days

related.text: The Mysteries Revised Edition, Chapter 3: Curious Common Magics (Art of Memory)

entries.title: Clan Ilfetu (Bjornaer clan and initiations)
entries.summary: Describes the Teach clan, the only one that initiates the House Mysteries, and lists its Clan Initiations (the Trial and Oath of the Prophet and the Deed of Honor) with the Virtues and Flaws gained.
quotes: To be a member of this clan, you must take the Clan Ilfetu Minor Virtue.
The Initiate is pinned under a large rock for 9 days and acquires the Visions Flaw

entries.title: Clan Maruhs (Bjornaer clan and initiations)
entries.summary: Describes the Strive clan and lists its Clan Initiations (the Trial of Chains, the Deed of Emulation and the Oath of the Muse) with the Virtues and Flaws each grants.
quotes: Bound by magical chains and cast into a pit

entries.title: Clan Midusulf (Bjornaer clan and initiations)
entries.summary: Describes the Lead clan and lists its Clan Initiations (the Trial of the Sacred Marriage, the Deed of Glory and the Oath of Steadfastness) with the Virtues and Flaws each grants.
quotes: The Initiate is ritually wedded to the earth through the letting of blood

entries.title: Clan Sirnas (Bjornaer clan and initiations)
entries.summary: Describes the Protect clan and lists its Clan Initiations (the Trial of Self Control, the Deed of the Woodland Warden and the Oath of the Helpful Stranger) with the Virtues and Flaws each grants.
quotes: The Initiate must starve himself until he collapses

entries.title: Clan Wilkis (Bjornaer clan and initiations)
entries.summary: Describes the Nourish clan and lists its Clan Initiations (the Trial of Self-Negation, the Deed of Fealty and the Oath of Completion) with the Virtues and Flaws each grants.
quotes: The Initiate must perform humiliating and degrading acts before many witnesses

entries.title: The Gathering of Twelve Years
entries.summary: Describes the twelve-yearly House gathering at Crintera where the Ritual of Twelve Years is performed and council seats are voted on, with advice for storyguides and an experience award for characters who attend.
quotes: All characters who attend a Gathering of Twelve Years should gain five experience points

related.text: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal

entries.title: The Apprenticeship of a Bjornaer Magus
entries.summary: Explains the two phases of Bjornaer training, the shared sleeping years under the whole sept and the awakened years under a single master after the heartbeast is awakened, and how this fits the Code of Hermes apprenticeship length.
quotes: an apprentice will receive 15 seasons of training over 15 years before joining the Order

entries.title: Bjornaer Magi and Shapeshifting Apprentices
entries.requires: House Bjornaer; character with Skinchanger or Shapeshifter Virtue
entries.summary: How each clan treats apprentices who can already shapeshift, and what a known shapeshifter must accept (the Secret Name Mystery first, and loss of the shapechanging Virtue as the Ordeal for the Inner Mystery). Suggests Dark Secret if the ability is hidden.

entries.title: Experiences of Apprenticeship (Bjornaer)
entries.summary: Shows how an apprenticeship differs depending on whether the child is found just before or just after a Gathering of Twelve Years, including how late the heartbeast awakens in the second case.

entries.title: Joining House Bjornaer
entries.requires: Hermetic magus of another House seeking to join House Bjornaer
entries.summary: The procedure and restrictions for a magus of another House who wants to join House Bjornaer. Candidates are adopted by a sept, then brought to the Ritual of Twelve Years; spell-free shapechangers, other House Initiates and those who ever bound a familiar are barred.
quotes: A magus cannot successfully complete the Ritual of Twelve Years if he has ever bound a familiar, even if the familiar is now dead.

entries.title: The Heartbeast (concept and Ritual of Twelve Years)
entries.requires: Virtue: Heartbeast (Ritual of Twelve Years, House Bjornaer)
entries.summary: Explains what the heartbeast is, that only the Ritual of Twelve Years grants the Heartbeast Virtue and Ability, and how it differs from magical shapechanging (a true animal, not a disguise). Also covers pregnancy, cross-species children and the House's bond of kinship.
quotes: Undergoing the Ritual of Twelve Years is the only way to gain the Heartbeast Virtue (and Ability)

related.text: ArM5 pp.91-92 Outer Mystery of House Bjornaer

entries.title: Choosing the Heartbeast
entries.summary: Advice for players on choosing a heartbeast that fits the character: expect physical signs, think about other Bjornaer in the troupe, and remember a magus can have only one.
quotes: Naturally, a magus can only have one heartbeast, for he only has a single spirit.

entries.title: Heartbeast Temperaments and Restrictions
entries.summary: Sorts heartbeasts into four temperaments, pure or aspected by another, and lists which creatures cannot be heartbeasts (domesticated animals, creatures with Might, those outside the Size limits). Includes the Size option for very small heartbeasts.
quotes: Creatures Smaller than a Weasel (Size –7)
Creatures Larger than an Aurochs (Size +3)

entries.title: Example Heartbeasts
entries.summary: Sidebar table assigning example animals to each heartbeast temperament and aspect.

entries.title: Plant Heartbeasts
entries.summary: Optional rule allowing an unusual plant 'heartbeast': the plant form can do only what a plant can do, and the character is likely to have Cyclic Magic.

entries.title: Changing Form (heartbeast)
entries.summary: A Bjornaer magus assumes his heartbeast form in a round, usually without a roll. A Stamina + Heartbeast roll is needed to overcome a shapechanging or magic-suppressing spell, and the animal form cannot cast.
quotes: making a Stamina + Heartbeast roll, against an Ease Factor of (3 + magnitude of the spell)

entries.title: Statistics of Shapechangers
entries.summary: Seven-step procedure for combining human and animal statistics for a shapechanged magus: Characteristics, Cunning versus Intelligence, Size, Virtues and Flaws, General Abilities, communication, and wounds and experience.
quotes: If the human and the animal Characteristic are both negative, use the lower of the two.
If the human and the animal Characteristic are both positive, use the higher of the two.

entries.title: Magical Items and Changing Form
entries.summary: Sidebar describing the standard item effect, Perceive the Change, that lets an item linked by a Linked Trigger respond when its holder takes animal form.
quotes: If this effect is instilled in a talisman, it can be made with Range Personal for a final level of 9.

entries.title: The Hidden Shape
entries.summary: Explains that, because of the Limit of Essential Nature, the heartbeast form appears to Hermetic magic as a mundane animal and has no ongoing effect after the transformation, though active magic on the magus can still be detected.

entries.title: Bjornaer Magi and Familiars
entries.summary: Initiation into the Heartbeast mystery makes it impossible to bind a familiar, and a magus who has ever bound one cannot complete the ritual.
quotes: Any magus who has ever bound a familiar, even if it has since died, cannot successfully complete the Ritual of Twelve Years

entries.title: Heartbeasts and Wizard's Twilight
entries.summary: What happens when a Bjornaer magus enters Twilight. Wizard's Twilight usually brings the heartbeast form, and Final Twilight yields a mundane beast or, with an Inner Mystery, a Great Beast with a Magic Might derived from the Heartbeast Ability.
quotes: acquires a Magic Might equal to (5 x Heartbeast Ability)

entries.title: The Magic of House Bjornaer
entries.summary: Notes on typical Bjornaer spell choices, such as heavy use of magical-sense Targets, and a rule that spells affecting a large heartbeast need a Size modifier.
quotes: Any spell that affects a heartbeast of Size +2 or greater must be invented with a Size modifier

entries.title: Characters of House Bjornaer (character creation)
entries.summary: Character creation guidance for a Bjornaer magus: choose the heartbeast first, then clan, with advice on Virtues and Flaws suited to the heartbeast and on why shapechanging Virtues are a hindrance in this House.

entries.title: Heartbeast (Supernatural Ability)
entries.summary: The Heartbeast Ability gives knowledge of the animal form, a Personality Trait named for the animal, and the power to change form. It cannot be learned from books and can only be taught by someone with the same temperament.
quotes: at a level equal to half the score in this Ability

entries.title: House Bjornaer: Harmonists, Wilderists, Clans and Septs
entries.summary: Background summary of House Bjornaer's two philosophical factions, its six clans and the role of septs, including clan Ilfetu's link to the Heartbeast initiation.

entries.title: Crintera's four-level heartbeast regio
entries.requires: Visiting Crintera (the House Bjornaer domus magna on Rugen)
entries.summary: Crintera lies in a four-level regio whose auras rise by level; as each boundary is crossed every visitor must resist a Corpus effect that brings out a heartbeast, first changing Personality Traits and then causing minor physical changes. Parma Magica and a Bjornaer Heartbeast roll can resist or shrug off the changes.
quotes: There are four levels to the magical regio, with auras of 1, 3, 5, and 8.
every character must resist a Corpus effect with a Penetration Total equal to the Ease Factor needed to see the next level
Of course, magi of House Bjornaer can shrug off these changes with a Heartbeast roll, should they want to.

entries.title: The Gathering of Twelve Years (House Bjornaer)
entries.summary: The House Bjornaer assembly held at Crintera every twelve years, when most initiations into the House's Mysteries take place. Includes advice for running the Gathering in a saga, including giving non-Bjornaer players a Bjornaer character for the event.
quotes: most initiations into the Mysteries of House Bjornaer are conducted during the gathering
The next gathering, due in 1227, is likely to be politically explosive

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages (House Bjornaer)

entries.title: Council of Elders and the Seats of Crintera (Bjornaer governance)
entries.summary: How the Council of Elders of Crintera is organized: six seats with fixed duties, how vacant seats are filled at the Gathering, the Primus's Seat of the Wolf, the reserved Senior Elder seat and its casting vote.
quotes: When an Elder dies or passes into Final Twilight, he will not be replaced until the next Gathering of Twelve Years.
The Senior Elder has the casting vote in any decision of the council

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages (House Bjornaer)

entries.title: Town Officials as a Virtue
entries.requires: Optional rule: Town Magistrate Social Status Virtue
entries.summary: Advises treating town office as part of a story, but offers a variant of the Town Magistrate Virtue for a general town official, with the Civil and Canon Law requirement and Academic Abilities benefit dropped.
quotes: a Virtue modeled upon the Minor Social Status Virtue: Town Magistrate (see Crime) can be used

entries.title: Shipka Pass Regio and Tribunal Site
entries.summary: Describes the regio chosen as the Transylvanian Tribunal meeting site, its custodian, the seven-year schedule of meetings, and how visitors and traders use the Promenades and Hall.
quotes: The Quaestiores selected the Shipka Pass regio as the Tribunal site.
Transylvanian Tribunals, held every seven years

entries.title: The Praeco of the Rhine Tribunal
entries.summary: Explains that unlike other Tribunals, where the oldest magus presides, the Rhine Tribunal's Praeco is by tradition the Primus of House Bonisagus.
quotes: but instead is always the Primus of House Bonisagus, who wields Bonisagus's voting sigil by proxy

entries.title: Tribunal Meetings (Hosting)
entries.summary: A covenant chosen by lot to host the Tribunal must provide a tournament site, an excellent Aegis of the Hearth and lavish hospitality, and risks financial ruin and Quaesitorial scrutiny.
quotes: The covenant is expected to provide a secluded area for the tournament, an excellent Aegis of the Hearth, and lavish hospitality.

entries.title: The Hermetic Polity
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Explains the split between executive power held by the citizens and administrative power held by the Council of Magistrates, and how prosecution and judgment of Code breaches differ from other Tribunals.
quotes: The citizens of the polity have all the executive power, whereas the Council of Magistrates has all the administrative power.

entries.title: Origins of the Polity (archai, archon, logothete, polemarch)
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Sidebar summarising the Athenian-style polity the Tribunal copies: magistrates chosen at random, serving for limited terms with no executive power, and the offices of archai, archon, logothete and polemarch.
quotes: a council of 16 magistrates who manage the Tribunal's resources, review the law, and investigate cases
Archai are selected at each Tribunal meeting, and serve for seven years at a time.

entries.title: Citizenship: politai and metoikoi
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Defines the two classes of magus in the Tribunal, citizens (politai) and resident foreigners (metoikoi), how civic duty is tracked with tokens, and who may hold office.
quotes: Only politai are entitled to become magistrates.
A foreign magus can become a polites through a citizenship decree of the Tribunal

entries.title: The Phylai (four tribes)
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Citizens are divided into four phylai by the covenant where they keep their sanctum, each represented by an equal number of archai; lists the four phylai and their covenants.
quotes: all its politai are divided into four phylai

entries.title: The Council of Magistrates
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Describes the archai as a duty rather than an honor: who serves, how terms are limited, when the Council meets, and how service is compensated with tokens.
quotes: There are 16 archai, four drawn from each of the four phylai
No citizen can serve two consecutive terms as arche

entries.title: Theban Quaesitores
entries.requires: House Guernicus in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Explains how the Tribunal's polity, not House Guernicus, investigates Code breaches and revises the Peripheral Code, leaving Quaesitores as legal experts and witnesses.
quotes: the polity (in the form of a board of magistrates, see later) conducts investigations into potential breaches of the Code of Hermes, rather than the Quaesitores

entries.title: The Archon
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: The archon is chosen by the archai from among themselves, chairs the Council, and holds the Praeco's duties; may serve more than once.
quotes: A magus can serve as archon more than once.

entries.title: The Polemarch
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: The polemarch is elected for ability to execute Wizard's Marches and enforce sentences, can award tokens to helpers, and uses Tribunal enchanted devices that restrain a magus.
quotes: There is no limit to the number of times an individual can serve as polemarch

entries.title: The Logothete
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: The permanent Chief Redcap who records Council business, keeps the token and shard records and assigns Redcaps; sets out when a new logothete is elected and how Redcaps are barred from votes and sortition.
quotes: The logothete is the Chief Redcap of the Theban Tribunal.

entries.title: The Boards of Magistrates
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Explains how the Judicial, Legislative and Conciliatory Boards are staffed, convened by citizen application, and what each handles, including interim Tribunals and certamen conventions.
quotes: nominally there are three members of each board, and seven members of the treasury council
The Peripheral Code states that a board must convene within six months of the request
the Judicial Board can also convene an interim Tribunal if they can gather together at least 12 magi from four different covenants

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Societates pp.90-93 (certamen, debate)

entries.title: The Treasury Council (apodektai)
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: The seven archai not on a board manage the Tribunal's vis, vis loans, collection of vis and Gifted children, and the tutoring of prospective apprentices.
quotes: This duty typically results in the discovery of about 15 apprentices in total every seven years.
The repayment of vis does not include interest, since usury is a sin.

entries.title: The Tribunal Meeting
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Overview of the septennial meeting on Delos: its four phases in fixed order and the rotation of the principal phyle that organises it.
quotes: It is divided into four phases, each of which fulfills a different state function.

entries.title: Pre-Tribunal Procedure
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: The organising phyle prepares the housing on Delos before the meeting.

entries.title: Selection of Archai Candidates
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Each phyle compiles its candidate list of eligible citizens; refusing consent when eligible costs a shard.
quotes: a magus who is eligible for selection but refuses consent is given one shard

entries.title: The Hermetic Assembly
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: First phase of the Tribunal: voting by sigils on Conciliatory Board decrees, where all magi present vote and a majority carries a decree.
quotes: All decrees are passed by a majority vote of those magi present.

entries.title: Decrees of Citizenship
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: How a metoikos petitions the Assembly for citizenship, with required contribution, resident covenant and an arche sponsor.
quotes: have at least one arche as sponsor

entries.title: The Nature of the Law
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: The Theban Code contains only deliberate legislation, with no precedent from earlier rulings.
quotes: Each case is judged according to the Code and with no reference to previous rulings.

entries.title: The Law Council
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Second phase: review of the Peripheral Code, debate between the two archai, and the option of a pre-emptive review of a law one expects to be convicted under.
quotes: if the alternative is accepted, the change to the Peripheral Code is recorded

entries.title: The People's Court
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Third phase: trial of Hermetic crimes with archai as prosecution and defense principals, a vote on guilt only, and the polemarch's power to prevent flight.
quotes: The polemarch is empowered by the Peripheral Code to prevent the flight of a guilty party by any means

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages pp.56-61

entries.title: Execution of Sentences
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Punishments are proposed in decreasing severity and voted on; shards accompany every conviction, tokens reward the prosecuting arche, and Marches never occur on Delos.
quotes: All punishments are accompanied by a penalty of three shards for a High Crime or one for a Low Crime.
A Wizard's March is never conducted on Delos

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.60

entries.title: Conduct of Archai
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Any citizen can accuse an arche or the polemarch of dereliction and propose a shard fine, decided by two votes.
quotes: a proposed fine of one to seven shards

entries.title: Sortition of Archai
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: How the new archai are drawn by lot from each phyle's candidate list and assigned to boards, and token payment for outgoing officers.
quotes: The logothete then selects four tokens from the jar at random

entries.title: Election of the Archon and Polemarch
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: The archai elect the archon by show of hands and then vote on nominated polemarch candidates; only a previous polemarch may refuse.
quotes: Only a magus who has already served as polemarch can refuse the role.

entries.title: The Tribunal Treasury on Delos
entries.summary: Describes the Tribunal's vis and artifact treasury, who holds its key, how it is guarded, and the spontaneous magical effects caused by the stored vis.
quotes: may only be opened with a large iron key that is entrusted to the archon

entries.title: Tribunal boundaries and joining a Tribunal
entries.requires: Saga option: expanding or redrawing Tribunal boundaries in the Nile region
entries.summary: Explains what a new covenant needs in order to join an existing Tribunal and how inter-Tribunal border disputes are settled at Grand Tribunal.
quotes: Inter-tribunal disputes, such as border definitions, must be settled at Grand Tribunal (ArM5, page 14).

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.49

entries.title: Founding a new Tribunal
entries.requires: Saga option: creating a Nile Tribunal
entries.summary: Sets out the minimum membership needed to found a new Tribunal and the steps and obstacles to getting it ratified at a Grand Tribunal.
quotes: A Tribunal must have at least twelve magi from at least four covenants, and at least one Quaesitor to preside at Tribunal meetings.

entries.title: Tremere Block Voting and Tribunal Tactics
entries.summary: Describes how Tremere magi vote as a bloc by proxying votes to the House Tribune, and the three tactics they use to reform the Peripheral Code: refining existing rulings, requesting reviews, and defining terms favorably.
quotes: The main tactics that Tremere magi use to reform the Peripheral Code are:

entries.title: House Tremere Structure and Ranks
entries.summary: Outlines the Tremere hierarchy of Primus, exarchs, experienced, skilled and newly Gauntleted magi, the decennial council of sigil-holding magi, and the principle that subordination is repaid with aid in loans of vis, money, books or items.
quotes: Members of the House do not have names for the ranks below exarch, but are aware they exist.

entries.title: The Role of Young Magi (Tremere Duties and Aid)
entries.summary: Describes the duties of young Tremere magi, including the call to arms, and the system of House aid they may draw on (one form of aid at a time, changing it takes a season in a multi-House covenant), with example loans, services and logistical support.
quotes: Assume a young magus may have one form of aid at a time and that it takes a complete season for a player character in a multi-house covenant to change his form of aid.
A younger magus generally loses a season per year to the work of the House, less if he completes his duties swiftly.

entries.title: The Role of Skilled Magi (Tremere Duties and Aid)
entries.summary: Missions and support available to skilled Tremere magi, such as larger loans of vis, widely-admired books, tame animals, hired groups and mercenaries; they may hold two types of support, each tradable for three of the young-magi level.
quotes: A magus at this level of skill can have two types of support from the list above.

entries.title: The Role of Experienced Magi (Tremere Duties and Aid)
entries.summary: Duties and resources of experienced Tremere magi, who act with little supervision: gifts of silver and vis, loans of major books and powerful items, warships or grogs; they select three forms of support, tradable for lower-level picks, and must justify spending with consistent success.
quotes: An experienced magus may select three forms of support from the list above.

entries.title: Material Aid in Your Saga
entries.summary: Advice for the troupe on negotiating and adjusting the level of House aid given to Tremere characters, treating aid as compensation for seasons lost to House service and tuning it to the saga's themes.
quotes: The system of aid also compensates Tremere magi for the seasons of study they lose in the service of their House.

entries.title: The Role of the Exarchs (Tremere Duties and Aid)
entries.summary: Lists the six exarchates, an exarch's duties, and the resources an exarch may command (vis, masterpiece books, extraordinary items, armies); three picks from the list, each tradable for three picks on the experienced magi list.
quotes: An exarch may choose three items from this list, each tradable for three picks on the experienced magi list

entries.title: Promotion by Force
entries.summary: Introduces the alternative promotion path in House Tremere: instead of being promoted politically, a magus may claim a rank by dueling, with the dishonor of using vis against other Tremere in such duels.
quotes: When dueling with other Tremere magi, it is dishonorable to use vis.

entries.title: Claiming the Name (Gauntlet by Certamen)
entries.summary: Explains the Tremere Gauntlet as a certamen challenge from apprentice to master for the title of magus, how it is staged and judged, and the ceremony of the birchwood wand that serves as the new magus's sigil.
quotes: It is all-but unheard of for an apprentice to win the role of magus by force

entries.title: Claiming the Sigil (Experienced Magus by Force)
entries.summary: How a Tremere magus challenges his parens for his own sigil (once at a chosen time, then at each Decennial), and the privileges of a young magus who holds his own sigil, including how aid is treated and trivial votes at Tribunal.
quotes: The protégé may challenge for their sigil, at a time of their choosing, once.
After this, the magus may challenge at every Decennial meeting of the House.

entries.title: Claiming the Tribunal's Dragon Banner (Exarch by Force)
entries.summary: How an exarch's heir is chosen by dueling and how any Tremere magus may challenge an exarch to certamen once, with restrictions on timing and the Primus's possible responses; includes the Addled Secutor story seed.
quotes: A magus may only challenge the exarch for his role once, and must not do so while the House faces rivals, at Tribunal for example.

entries.title: Dissent (House Tremere)
entries.summary: Describes how the House handles periods of dissent, the mechanisms for healing rifts, and how dissent reduces the support available to player characters from different parts of the House.
quotes: In a time of dissent, most members of the House pretend that the structure is still functioning normally.

entries.title: Claiming the Sigil of Tremere (Primus by Force)
entries.summary: The process by which a Primus is replaced: succession by the legatus on retirement or death, and the Decennial duels among councilors to name a secutor who may challenge the Primus, with limits on repeated challenges.
quotes: The secutor may challenge the Primus as often as he wishes.

entries.title: Tremere Magical Mounts and Animals (Parma over Mounts)
entries.summary: Describes the House's use of trained and magical animals, and a rule on mounts: a mount only gains Magic Resistance if the Parma is extended over it, leaving either the mount undefended or the magus's own protection halved.
quotes: It's not possible to grant a mount Magic Resistance, except by extending the Parma over it.

entries.title: Tremere Virtues and Flaws Guidance
entries.summary: House-specific character creation notes: all Tremere magi have a Minor Magical Focus in Certamen, plus which Virtues are common or inappropriate and which Flaws the House would not accept or would see as embarrassing.
quotes: All Tremere magi have a Minor Magical Focus in Certamen.

entries.title: Tremere Abilities
entries.summary: Lists the Abilities Tremere magi value for crisis and peacetime, such as Intrigue, Bargain, Penetration, Concentration, Parma Magica, Survival, Swim and Leadership.
quotes: Younger magi are expected to be able to fend for themselves on the Wizard's March

entries.title: Tremere Specialist Roles
entries.summary: Introduces the specialist roles in which Tremere magi are trained to serve the House, noting that they cannot have magical focuses other than certamen and so hire other Houses for specialized research and item construction.
quotes: Tremere magi cannot have magical focuses other than certamen, so they hire magi from other Houses to provide specialized services.

entries.title: Co-option
entries.summary: Describes how House Tremere gets others to want what it wants and lists the key political tools (Advocacy, Aiding Emulants, Always Keeping Deals, Defining Normal, Direct Acculturation, Information, Latin, Non-Hermetic Actors, Prosperity) a character can use to lead on issues.
quotes: House Tremere coopts when it can, acting either as leader on an issue, or supporting those magi who are working toward a co-interest.
Players trying to use their characters as leaders on issues should familiarize themselves with the key tools used by House Tremere.

entries.title: House Tremere Reputation (Soft Power)
entries.summary: Optional rule: the troupe may set a Reputation score for House Tremere for characters acting on its behalf, which rises as soft-power stories succeed and falls through foolish or unjustified acts.
quotes: The troupe may to select a Reputation score for House Tremere which a character acting on the House's behalf may use.

entries.title: Tremere Apprentices
entries.summary: Describes the House Tremere custom of exchanging apprentices between Transylvania and frontier Tribunals so that each spends time in the other setting.
quotes: An apprentice must spend at least some time in Transylvania, to understand the value of what the House is building.

entries.title: Rotations and Decennials
entries.summary: Explains the Tremere expectation of regular returns to Transylvania and the Decennial planning meeting at Coeris, with advice on how a troupe can handle a magus's rotation using a reskinned replacement character.
quotes: At minimum, every Tremere magus should spend at least a season every ten years in Transylvania, unless kept abroad by pressing duties.
The easiest way to do this is just to reskin the primary magus (create a new character who looks and sounds different, but has the same underlying numbers).

entries.title: Beloved Rivals (Tytalan Formal Rivalry)
entries.summary: Describes the Tytalan custom of formally declaring a lifelong rivalry, how it is declared and what it commits the rivals to, and the formal modes of address that tell other Tytali not to interfere.
quotes: Beloved Rivals most commonly exist between master and pupil, but could potentially exist between any pair of Tytali who have sufficient cause.

entries.title: Eristic Moots
entries.summary: Explains the eristic moot, a public dispute between Tytalan magi: who may attend, how the permitted weapons (debate, combat, certamen, magic) are agreed in advance, and the two special moots, the Apprentice's Gauntlet and the choice of a new Primus.
quotes: By convention, the minimum attendance for an eristic moot is five

entries.title: Tytalan Apprenticeship
entries.summary: Describes how House Tytalus trains apprentices, from the education before opening the Arts through the harsh years of training and the Book of Instruction, and what happens to apprentices who fail to react to it.
quotes: During the next 15 years, the apprentice's life is exceptionally hard.

entries.title: The Apprentice's Gauntlet
entries.summary: How a Tytalan apprenticeship ends: the apprentice must force his master to accept him as a magus in an eristic moot, with consequences (Self Confident, Weak Parens, Tormenting Master) depending on how and when the Gauntlet is passed.
quotes: The apprentice passes his Gauntlet if he can make his master accept him as an equal.
An apprentice who succeeds in killing his master at any point in his apprenticeship is elevated to the status of magus immediately, regardless of the state of his training.

entries.title: Joining House Tytalus
entries.summary: Explains how a magus of another House or a hedge wizard can become Tytalus by forcing a Tytalan magus to accept him, that dual membership is allowed only here, and how a magus leaves the House.
quotes: Of course, since House Tytalus is the only one of the 12 Houses that permit dual membership

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages, House Guernicus

entries.title: Tytalan Cabals
entries.summary: Describes how Tytalan cabals are formed and run: anonymous invitations, disguised attendance, an inaugural meeting, consensus tasking and closed membership.
quotes: A cabal is usually initiated by a single magus, who decides that he needs support in completing a specific goal.

entries.title: Leper Magus (Vis from Leprotic Wounds)
entries.requires: House Tytalus; Virtue: Leper Magus (requires Flaw: Leprosy)
entries.summary: A Major Hermetic Virtue whose extended mechanic lets a leper magus take a wound to generate vis for one spell or lab activity, with limits on recovery, aging and how often it can be used.
quotes: By accepting a Light Wound, the magus can infuse a single magical working with three pawns of vis, of any Technique or Form.
A wound taken in this fashion must heal completely before the power may be used again, and any character using this power more than three times a year must make an extra Aging roll in winter.

entries.title: Titanoi (Mystery Cult of House Tytalus)
entries.summary: Describes the Titanoi cult of spirit summoners: the Major Magical Focus in Spirits and Abilities taught in apprenticeship, and the Mystery Virtues the cult can initiate.
quotes: The cult can Initiate the following Virtues: Hermetic Theurgy, Invocation Magic, Names of Power, Theurgic Spirit Familiar, and Student of Magic Realm.

entries.title: Leper Magi (Magi Aegroti)
entries.requires: House Tytalus; Virtue: Leper Magus; Flaw: Leprosy
entries.summary: Describes the lineage of leper magi, how later generations are found among lepers, their place in the Order, and the Virtues, Flaws and Magical Focus all of them have.
quotes: All magi aegroti must buy the Leper Magus Virtue and the Leprosy Flaw.

entries.title: The Curse of Leprosy
entries.summary: Explains leprosy as a Divine Curse in Mythic Europe and the legal and social restrictions the Office of the Seclusion places on lepers.
quotes: It cannot be cured, and is only contracted by those who are spiritually impure.

related.text: City & Guild, Chapter 1: Towns & Cities, Disease

entries.title: Infernal Taint (Goetic Arts in the Titanoi)
entries.summary: Optional storyguide rule that the Titanoi mystagogues can also initiate the Goetic Arts as Major Mystery Virtues and teach Goetic Spell Mastery, with the social and supernatural taint that carries.
quotes: At the option of the storyguide, the Mystagogues of the Titanoi can also Initiate the Goetic Arts of Summoning, Ablating, Binding, and Commanding as Major Mystery Virtues, and teach Goetic Spell Mastery.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal, Chapter 11: Ars Goetia

entries.title: Tytalus Cabals
entries.summary: Explains Tytalus cabals: anonymous clandestine groups formed to pursue a specific tactical goal, whose members may each have different motives.
quotes: to do so they form clandestine organizations called cabals

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Societates, House Tytalus

entries.title: Tytalus Primus Succession and the Two Primi
entries.summary: States how a Tytalus Primus claims the title and describes the current dispute between two Primi, the three ways it could end, and the approach of the Grand Tribunal as a crisis point.
quotes: The condition of Primus-hood for House Tytalus is that one magus must force the others to accept his right to lead.

entries.title: The Tytalus Traitor
entries.summary: A voluntarily exiled Tytalus magus who counts as having lost every conflict and is an untouchable foe in House games. The Traitor's one duty is to restart stalled House conflicts, and they are often placed as Quaesitores or hoplites.
quotes: The Traitor has a single obligation to House Tytalus: to restart the House's conflicts if they stall.

entries.title: Ranks of Magi Bonisagi
entries.summary: Magi Bonisagi hold one of four research-based ranks, each with different duties and privileges (such as contributing a sigil to the Colentes pouch or being subject to the Primus's research commands). Rank is determined by House Acclaim.
quotes: There are four ranks for magi Bonisagi.

related.text: House Acclaim: Status in House Bonisagus

entries.title: Colentes Arcanorum
entries.summary: The five-member Bonisagus council, chosen at random from magi of cannophori rank or higher, that collects submitted Lab Texts and tractatus and compiles them into folios. Includes the chance that a character is selected and the council's powers over the Primus.
quotes: a player character who has achieved the rank of cannophori has a 1 in 5 chance of being selected

entries.title: Submitted Texts (Colentes)
entries.summary: How many Lab Texts and tractatus a Colens receives during a term, what they look for, and how long it takes to judge a submission.
quotes: It takes a day for Colens Arcanorum to briefly scan a submitted text and determine its value.

entries.title: Tenentes Occultorum
entries.requires: House Bonisagus (magi Trianomae); Minor Status Virtue: Tenens Occultorum
entries.summary: The four seasonal Trianomae officers who guard House secrets and watch mundane seekers of arcane lore, each responsible for a set of Tribunals. Explains how a character can begin play as a Tenens.

related.text: Ars Magica 5th Edition p.32 After Apprenticeship

entries.title: Colloquium Delectorum
entries.summary: The seven-yearly meeting at which the Colentes and Tenentes compile their findings, choose research for the next folio, and can be petitioned about the Primus's orders.

entries.title: The Primus of House Bonisagus
entries.summary: The Primus's powers (agenda-setting at Tribunals, selecting the councils, directing a magus's research) and the qualifications a candidate for Primus must meet.

entries.title: Apprentices of House Bonisagus
entries.summary: How House Bonisagus apprentices are chosen and trained, and the distinct gauntlets of the two branches: the Theoretical Interview for magi Bonisagi and a solo journey for magi Trianomae.

entries.title: Taking Another Magus's Apprentice
entries.summary: Magi of House Bonisagus alone may take another Hermetic magus's apprentice; the text lists informal House guidelines for using the right and the possible consequences (low crime charges, Wizard War), and notes that rank helps in finding an apprentice.
quotes: Unique among the Lineages, magi of House Bonisagus may take another Hermetic magus

entries.title: Fostering Apprentices
entries.summary: Magi Bonisagi swap apprentices for a year of Ability training and then a stint of lab assistance, a procedure that gives both apprentices Teaching and Profession: Scribe and improves Latin and Magic Theory.
quotes: At the end of two years, both apprentices should have scores of 2 in Teaching and Profession: Scribe, as well as improved scores in Latin and Magic Theory.

entries.title: The Cipher of Trianoma
entries.requires: House Bonisagus (magi Trianomae); others may decode
entries.summary: How magi of other lineages decipher the shorthand used by magi Trianomae, either by treating a cipher Lab Text as any other or by making a roll against a secret note.
quotes: To decode Trianoma's cipher you make an Intelligence + Latin + stress die roll.
Having decoded a previous cipher adds 3 to your decoding rolls.

entries.title: House Acclaim: Status in House Bonisagus
entries.summary: A community-based Reputation that every magus Bonisagi starts with, which grows through finished and published laboratory research and moves the magus up the House ranks. Describes how Acclaim points accrue and are sped up by being included in a folio.
quotes: House Acclaim is a free Reputation that every magus Bonisagi character receives at character generation.
The lucky author gains twice the Acclaim points listed on the following table if his research is included in a folio.

entries.title: Research and Acclaim Points
entries.summary: Table of how many Acclaim points each kind of laboratory achievement (tractatus, summae, spells, talismans, familiars, apprentices, Breakthroughs and so on) is worth, with a note on how rank affects fostering and gauntlets.
quotes: Write an Art tractatus
Stabilize a Breakthrough

entries.title: House Acclaim Points and Score
entries.summary: Table converting Acclaim points into an Acclaim score and rank title, plus the uses of the score: social bonuses within the House, a bonus to resist magi Trianomae, and a bonus to the roll to find an apprentice.
quotes: to any social skill roll involving her Presence characteristic when interacting with another magus of House Bonisagus
You may add your Acclaim score to your roll to find an apprentice

entries.title: Redcaps: Status and Role in the Order
entries.summary: Explains what a Redcap is: an unGifted member of House Mercere with the rights and privileges of a magus, a sigil, and a tradition of not voting at Tribunal, who acts like a Hermetic companion serving magi and performing duties magi find beneath them.
quotes: Redcaps may not have the Gift, but they do have full rights and privileges

entries.title: Messengers and Heralds (Mercer Houses, Registration, Redcap Pay)
entries.summary: How the Redcap courier network works: Mercer Houses in each Tribunal, the duty to distribute Tribunal invitations, covenant and vis-source registration, message delivery times, blacklisting, and the customary payment Redcaps receive from each covenant they visit.
quotes: House Mercere's only official obligation to Tribunal is the charge to distribute invitations before the gathering
Redcaps are traditionally paid in silver by the covenants they visit on their rounds.

entries.title: Societas Merceris: Followers of Belin
entries.requires: Redcap society: Followers of Belin (Legacy flaw)
entries.summary: A Redcap society of elite messengers descended from or adopted into Belin's line, with character requirements limiting them to humble, diligent Personality traits and the Legacy flaw.
quotes: they must take the Legacy flaw (see the Appendix, Virtues and Flaws)

entries.title: Societas Merceris: the Pawnbrokers
entries.summary: A Redcap society that stores vis in distinctively shaped tokens; members may trade starting magic item levels for vis in their signature shape and receive a yearly pawn of vis from the House.
quotes: Pawnbroker Redcaps may trade two levels of their starting magic items for a pawn of vis in their signature shape

entries.title: Mercenaries and Guardians (Custodians, Bounties, Portal Guards, Fine Collection)
entries.summary: Describes custodial Redcaps who guard other Redcaps, claim bounties on road threats, guard Mercere's Portals for a share of tolls, investigate and spy, and collect fines and damages for a percentage of the value.
quotes: one pawn of vis per use
he is given one-tenth its value from House funds

entries.title: Societas Merceris: the Bloodcaps
entries.requires: Redcap society: Bloodcaps (Faerie Blood or Strong Faerie Blood, plus a Malediction)
entries.summary: A Redcap society of faerie-blooded border guards; members must take Faerie Blood and a Greater or Lesser Malediction triggered by the cross or scripture, and tend to carry combat-oriented magic items.
quotes: All Bloodcaps must take Faerie Blood (or Strong Faerie Blood)

entries.title: Errant Redcaps (Duty and Sanctions)
entries.summary: Covers how the House handles Redcaps who neglect their service: reporting to the senior Redcap, rewards of magic items and longevity potions for the dutiful, allowances for lost seasons, and the ultimate sanction of being declared an orphan and cast out.
quotes: The ultimate sanction is to declare the Redcap an orphan ("Orbus"), throwing him out of the House.

entries.title: Societas Merceris: the Goliards
entries.requires: Redcap society: Goliards (Clerk or Educated, plus a Compulsion)
entries.summary: An artistic, hedonistic Redcap society; members must take Clerk or Educated and a Compulsion toward an inspirational vice, and commonly take Free Expression, Inspirational or a Hermetic Patron.
quotes: characters must take either Clerk or Educated

entries.title: Magical Merceres (Mercere Magi Privileges and Creation)
entries.summary: Describes Gifted Mercere magi: their lineage expectations, privileges (contracts for items, interest-free vis loans, free Portal use, support from Mercer Houses), yearly messenger season, casting taboos and the free Virtue they take at creation.
quotes: starting Mercere magi always take either Puissant Art (Creo) or Puissant Art (Muto) as their free Virtue
They may borrow up to 10p of vis from their House without paying interest

entries.title: Mercurian Magi (Cult of Mercury Lineage)
entries.requires: House Mercere (Mercurian lineage / Cult of Mercury)
entries.summary: Describes the Mercurian lineage of Mercere magi, who preserve Cult of Mercury practices and have access to a set of Mercurian spell mastery abilities listed in the Laboratory appendix.
quotes: They include: Adaptive Casting, Ceremonial Casting, Disguised Casting, Lab Mastery, Learn from Mistakes, and Stalwart Casting.

entries.title: Societas Merceris: the Cult of Heroes
entries.requires: Redcap society: Cult of Heroes (Blood of Heroes for hero characters; Mythic Blood or Mercurian Magic and Pagan for magi)
entries.summary: A society that raises exceptional children as heroes; hero characters take the Blood of Heroes virtue, may trade starting magic item levels for Characteristic increases, and Cult magi may substitute Mastered Spells for Puissant Art.
quotes: Either type may exchange 10 levels of effects in their starting magic items for a +1 increase to any of their negative Characteristics.

entries.title: Societas Merceris: Milvi Antiquiti
entries.requires: Redcap society: Milvi Antiquiti (Mutantum Magic for magi)
entries.summary: A Mutantes society that copies and lends ancient books to magi for a vis fee and carries them by shapeshifting into birds; magi members take Mutantum Magic and Redcap members usually learn Latin, Scribe and Magic Theory.
quotes: usually 1p a season or 3p a year

entries.title: Mercere's Portals (Lab Activity)
entries.requires: House Mercere (Mercere magi; season studying an existing Portal)
entries.summary: How a Mercere magus builds a Portal: study an existing one for a season, enchant two linked archways with a Rego Terram effect, then perform a connecting ceremony in both locations; completed Portals cannot be moved.
quotes: each with an instilled effect of Rego Terram, level 65 (base level 35, +4 Arc; +10 for Unlimited uses)

entries.title: The Hermetic Tourney
entries.summary: Overview of the seven-yearly Tourney: who may enter, team size limits, the entry stake for outside teams, and the six traditional events.
quotes: Each team that does not represent one accepted Normandy covenant must stake five pawns of vis per magi to enter
Teams are limited to a maximum of five members, excluding grogs and companions.

entries.title: Winning the Tourney (Scoring)
entries.summary: Points scoring for each Tourney event, tie-breaking by seniority, the named finishing ranks, and the Hermetic Reputation granted for achieving them.
quotes: A team receives a starting tally equal to the number of members of their covenant
The team winning the hastiludium receives 20 points, the defeated finalist 10 points, and the other semifinalists five points each.
Any covenant achieving one of the named ranks in the Tourney has an appropriate Hermetic Reputation of level 2 for the next seven years.

entries.title: Tourney Events (General Rules)
entries.summary: Sidebar introducing the events: an even number of registered teams, and the hosting covenant's own event to be declared by the previous summer solstice.
quotes: Tradition and the rules demand there must always be an even number of teams in the tournament.

entries.title: The Hastiludium
entries.summary: Tourney event where teams of three magi on improvised magical mounts use spells to force opponents off and push their mount past the other team's line.
quotes: Each magus may cast a single spell before the contest begins in order to prepare, and may then cast magic freely during the contest.
Parma Magica may not be extended over the mounts, but both sides may freely cast magic on either mount.

entries.title: The Certamen Tournament
entries.summary: Knockout certamen event in which the older magus chooses the Technique and the younger the Form, with a team champion picked each round.
quotes: The older magus chooses the Technique, the younger the Form.

entries.title: The Joust
entries.summary: Mounted knockout event between single champions, best of three, where magic may affect only one's own person, mount or weapons; the Tourney's most dangerous event.
quotes: The winner is the magus who prevails in a best of three match

entries.title: The Melee
entries.summary: Non-magical team contest for grogs and companions to capture opposing Creo Imaginem circle castles using blunt weapons; seriously injuring an opponent forfeits the contest.
quotes: Three grog or companion champions for each team attempt to charge across the field
damage is fatigue unless botched

entries.title: The Dimicatio
entries.summary: House Flambeau's duel in which champions cast forceless spells at each other and defend with fast-cast defenses; penetrating the opponent's Parma is foul play.
quotes: Each magus uses a fast-cast defense (ArM5, page 83) to try to block the opposing spell. The first magus whose spell reaches his opponent's Parma is the winner.

entries.title: The Hosting Covenant's Choice
entries.summary: The sixth Tourney event is chosen by the host covenant and must be a true test of magical ability.
quotes: It must be a true test of magical ability, but beyond that may take any form.

entries.title: Tourney Prizes
entries.summary: How prize pawns are spent in rank order on tropaea, books, items and entrance-fee vis, with conversion rates between prize pawns and Build Points.
quotes: Calculate this as 1 prize pawn per 5 Build Points of the book.
One prize pawn may be traded for an immediate once-only selection of 5 pawns of Form vis, or three pawns of Technique vis.

entries.title: Tourney Ranks & Prizes (Table)
entries.summary: Table of prize pawns awarded for each finishing rank, with advice on adjusting it for richer or poorer sagas.
quotes: The prizes listed in this table assume at least 200 pawns worth of prizes are available in total, and 24 teams entering.

entries.title: The Hermetic Landscape (Tribunal-Owned Vis and the Tourney)
entries.summary: Overview of how vis outside covenant grounds belongs to the whole Normandy Tribunal and is leased out through a seven-yearly Tourney that also awards books and other resources.
quotes: all vis that does not originate from within the grounds of a covenant was declared to be the property of the Tribunal as a whole rather than of any specific individual covenant

entries.title: The Perthean Compact
entries.summary: Introduces the Peripheral Code rulings that make all Normandy vis sources the property of covenants and sort them into seisins, legacies, tropaea and luctationes.
quotes: The Perthean Compact revolves around the ruling that all vis sources, whether they are exclusive access in perpetuity or a fixed term lease, belong to covenants, not to individuals. It categorizes vis sources into four types: seisins, legacies, tropaea, and luctationes.

entries.title: Seisins (and Cursor Travel Distance)
entries.summary: A vis source within a day's return march of a covenant's council chamber is automatically that covenant's seisin with exclusive harvest rights; includes the test of proving the distance with a cursor and a rule of thumb for miles covered per day.
quotes: A seisin recognized by the Tribunal grants its owners exclusive right of harvest.

if a man can get from the covenant's council chamber to a vis source and back again, on his own two feet and unaided by magic, between sunrise and sunset on a day which is within a month of an equinox, then the vis source is a seisin of that covenant
10 + (2 x Athletics) cross country

entries.title: Legacies
entries.summary: A newly found vis source too far to be a seisin can be a legacy lease held by its discoverer for seven years, renewable only by Tribunal vote; poaching from a legacy is a High Crime.
quotes: the terms of the lease last only seven years
the offender is automatically found guilty of the High Crime of depriving a magus of his magical power

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.59

entries.title: Tricks and Cheats (Seisin Manipulation)
entries.summary: Sidebar on how covenants bend seisin rules: remote council chambers, unchallenged assumed distances, and altering terrain to make or unmake a seisin.
quotes: a claim that remains uncontested stays a seisin until challenged.

entries.title: Tropaea
entries.summary: Easily harvested vis sources that are neither seisins nor legacies belong to the Tribunal and are leased for seven years to Tourney winners; founding a covenant near one needs Tribunal approval.
quotes: Tropaea are to be distributed among the members of the Tribunal on seven-year leases by being won in the Tourney.

entries.title: Luctationes
entries.summary: Tribunal-owned vis sources that need skill or risk to harvest are open contests for any magus each year, confer no lasting rights, and cost no Build Points unless a covenant has exclusive access.
quotes: If a covenant does have exclusive access to a luctatio for some reason, then it is costed as a vis source with the Contested Resource Hook.

entries.title: Interim Leases and Plundering
entries.summary: Procedure for claiming a newly found vis source through a Quaesitor's interim lease, and the Low Crime of plundering for harvesting without one.
quotes: A covenant which harvests a hitherto unknown vis source but chooses not to secure an interim lease is guilty of plundering, a Low Crime under the Peripheral Code of the Normandy Tribunal.

entries.title: The Perthean Compact and Personal Vis Sources
entries.requires: Normandy Tribunal; Hermetic Virtue granting a personal vis source
entries.summary: Explains how a magus's own bodily vis is exempt from the Perthean Compact and how a character with an external personal vis source can justify it in a Normandy saga.
quotes: any vis that is generated by the person of a magus (in his hair, blood, and so forth) is the sole possession of that magus, and not subject to the Perthean Compact

entries.title: Eremites and Coenobites
entries.summary: Solitary magi (eremites) and communities that fail the vis requirement (coenobia) cannot hold seisins and must rely on Tourney tropaea and luctationes, competing as individuals.
quotes: An eremite is forbidden by the Peripheral Code from owning a seisin, and he must rely upon tropaeum leases won at the Tourney or attending luctatio for his vis supply.

entries.title: House Bjornaer
entries.summary: House overview with the rules-relevant points: every Bjornaer magus has a heartbeast form as the House's Outer Mystery, and Bjornaer magi cannot form the links needed for a familiar.
quotes: Bjornaer magi are unable to forge the necessary links to have a familiar

entries.title: House Guernicus
entries.summary: House overview covering the Quaesitores, the Order's investigators and judges, who customarily receive vis for their work, and the Hoplites who support them. Only a character trained in House Guernicus can start play as a Quaesitor.
quotes: A starting maga can only be a Quaesitor if she was trained in House Guernicus.
the custom of the Order is that the Quaesitors be given a few pawns of vis as a gift

entries.title: House Mercere
entries.summary: House overview covering the Redcaps: all Mercere count as members of the Order whether or not they have The Gift, and unGifted Redcaps attend Tribunals but only vote if Gifted.
quotes: regardless of whether they possess The Gift, are officially recognized as magi of the Order.
Redcaps are permitted to attend Hermetic Tribunals, but by convention they only vote if they have The Gift.

entries.title: House Tremere
entries.summary: House overview with the Tremere custom of holding apprentices' voting sigils until they defeat their parens in certamen, which concentrates the House's votes in few hands.
quotes: until the filius beats the parens in certamen, or until the parens dies

entries.title: House Bjornaer Lore (Arcane Ability)
entries.summary: The Organization Lore for House Bjornaer, which also governs its Mystery rites. Each season spent initiating a Mystery gives experience in it.
quotes: every time a magus spends a season initiating a Mystery, he gains experience in House Bjornaer Lore from exposure

entries.title: House Acclaim
entries.summary: Flambeau's free Hermetic Reputation measuring prestige: gained through witnessed deeds, lost through inactivity or ignoble acts, never below zero.
quotes: House Acclaim is a free Reputation that every Flambeau magus gains at the start of play.
Loss of House Acclaim is handled by taking away experience points instead of adding them.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.21 House Acclaim (Bonisagus)

entries.title: Example Acclaim Awards
entries.summary: Table of sample experience-point awards and penalties in House Acclaim for tournaments, certamen, Wizard's War, slaying beasts and renegades, and inactivity.

entries.title: Bonisagus House Acclaim (Conciatta's Virtues)
entries.summary: States how many House Acclaim points a Bonisagus magus earns for rediscovering each of Conciatta's Virtues.
quotes: rediscovering Conciatta's Minor Virtues awards 15 acclaim points each

entries.title: Verditius Limit on Sales to Mundanes
entries.summary: Since the Order restricted direct sales of enchanted devices to mundane society, House Verditius limits each member to a set number of items sold to mundanes per year, sold through unGifted intermediaries; sales to Hermetic magi are unlimited and Tribunals may modify the limit.
quotes: The number was set at one magical item per year, and the selling maga must use her network of intermediaries during the exchange.

entries.title: Guardians of the Forests (Rhine Peripheral Code Ruling)
entries.summary: Describes a Rhine Tribunal ruling letting a recognized guardian of a forest do otherwise forbidden things in its defense, how guardian status becomes official only if the Tribunal accepts the claim, and why it does not apply outside the Rhine.

related.text: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal p.18

entries.title: Mundane Interference (Masks)
entries.summary: Normandy treats meddling with mundanes as an offense only once mundane reprisals harm Hermetic victims, so covenants act through masks; masks give no protection against depriving other magi of their power.
quotes: Masks provide no protection from charges of depriving other magi of their power, so they cannot legally be used against the senex of a town.

entries.title: Mundane Interference (Tribunal Ruling)
entries.summary: No specific rulings exist on agencies and masks, but the Tribunal rarely convicts when damage to a Hermetic magus cannot be clearly demonstrated.
quotes: the Tribunal rarely convicts in situations where damage to a Hermetic magus cannot be unequivocally demonstrated.

entries.title: Further Excerpts from the Normandy Peripheral Code
entries.summary: Dated precedents of the Normandy Tribunal covering court wizardry, borders, raids, deprivation of magical power, covert healing and mundane interference.
quotes: Quaesitor Lothaire ruled that raiding magi are forbidden from damaging the physical structure of a covenant

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Societates, House Ex Miscellanea

entries.title: Atsingani: Council Chamber Fixed by Tribunal Custom
entries.summary: A mobile covenant with no native aura is nonetheless bound by Tribunal custom to keep a fixed council chamber, which Quaesitors may check, and which also supplies its only stable vis.
quotes: The Tribunal's customs forbid them from moving their council chamber

entries.title: Chapter Houses and Cenobites in Normandy
entries.summary: Shows how the Normandy Peripheral Code treats an outside covenant's chapter house: it is not recognized, so a lone resident magus is a cenobite, and recognition may come only over time.
quotes: Chapter houses are not recognized under the Peripheral Code in the Normandy Tribunal, so the single magus who lives in the Cherbourg covenant is considered a cenobite.

related.text: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal p.82

entries.title: The Oak Gild (Eichengilde)
entries.summary: The largest and oldest Rhine gild, devoted to tradition, respect for the Founders and elders, and shunning outside wisdom, and led by the Prima of Bonisagus.

entries.title: The Hawthorn Gild (Weissdorngilde)
entries.summary: The smallest and one of the oldest Rhine gilds, which seeks to protect wild places and creatures from mundanes and is dominated by Bjornaer Wilderists.

entries.title: The Ash Gild (Eschengilde)
entries.summary: An aggressive, magically powerful gild favoring dominion over the magi's lands and open dealing with mundanes, with a hidden focus on combating the Order of Odin.

entries.title: The Elder Gild (Holundergilde)
entries.summary: A gild, largely of Merinita magi, devoted to preserving the fae and promoting friendly contact between magi and faeries.

entries.title: The Linden Gild (Lindengilde)
entries.summary: A small, altruistic go-between gild founded after the Schism War to build trust and peaceful resolution between magi and covenants.

entries.title: The Apple Gild (Apfelgilde)
entries.summary: The newest and weakest Rhine gild, advocating peaceful relations with and acceptance in the mundane world.

entries.title: Gild Alliances and Tribunal Politics
entries.summary: Describes which Rhine gilds ally with or oppose each other and the main fault line between wilderness-minded and mundane-minded magi.

entries.title: Asclepius and the Privileges of the Coloniae
entries.summary: Lists what coloniae (young settler magi from other Tribunals) may expect and may not do under their privilege, including office, apprentices and visitors.
quotes: The coloniae, or settlers, are young magi from other Tribunals permitted to develop underutilized sections of the Tribunal, under tight agreements.

entries.title: Triumph of Asclepius
entries.summary: Describes the annually elected leadership of the Covenant of Asclepius and the yearly payment and minor duties that go with it.
quotes: This includes 16 pawns of vis, three pounds of pure gold, six requested books copied from a certain library, a fine dinner, and several other minor tokens of esteem.

entries.title: Coeris and the Privileges of the Cives
entries.requires: Privilege: cives (Covenant of Coeris), automatic for House Tremere
entries.summary: Lists what citizens (cives) of the Covenant of Coeris are permitted and required to do, including House Tremere's assistance, standing for any office, and selecting the aedile.
quotes: A cives, or citizen, is usually a Tremere magus living as a Tremere magus should.

entries.title: Domostron and the Privileges of the Socii
entries.summary: Lists what socii (allied non-Tremere magi such as Redcaps, Quaesitores and hoplites) may do and must do under their privilege, including office, support and aedile selection.
quotes: All Redcaps, Quaestiores, and dedicated hoplites are automatically socii, if they are not civitates.

entries.title: Diodorus and the Privileges of the Hospites
entries.summary: Lists what hospites (magi hired to practise particular skills for House Tremere) may expect and which actions need permission, such as new apprentices, familiars and talismans.
quotes: Hospites are usually required to seek permission before:
They have few rights, but are paid well for their services.

entries.title: Pannonia and the Privileges of the Foederati
entries.summary: Describes foederati, magi of foreign covenants admitted to the Tribunal under individually negotiated agreements, and the usual rights and permission requirements in those agreements.
quotes: Foederati have individually negotiated agreements, but usually they include the right to:

entries.title: Legalities of Residency
entries.summary: Explains why a magus's privilege is rarely challenged as against the Code, that leaving the Tribunal is allowed, and the competing legal views on whether a broken privilege must be repaid.
quotes: A magus can leave the Tribunal at any time.

entries.title: Magic for the Debating Arena
entries.summary: Covers using magic during Tribunal debates, how the Order frowns on it, and how self-enhancing spells can add bonuses to particular debate Defense Totals.
quotes: granting a +3 bonus to all debating Defense Totals that use the Leadership Ability

related.text: ArM5 p.145 Aura of Ennobled Presence

entries.title: The Process in Brief (Fourth Estate)
entries.requires: Saga arc: Order of Hermes as the Fourth Estate
entries.summary: Outlines the sequence of steps a covenant follows to move the Order toward integration with mundane society, from test cases at Tribunal through negotiation with nobles and Church to the Grand Tribunal.

entries.title: A Life's Work (pacing the Fourth Estate)
entries.requires: Saga arc: Order of Hermes as the Fourth Estate
entries.summary: Suggests measuring the pace of the integration saga in Tribunal meetings, with a fair-pace schedule of what happens at each successive Tribunal.
quotes: With Tribunals held every seven years and a Grand Tribunal every 33 years

entries.title: Preparing for Tribunal Debate
entries.requires: Saga arc: Order of Hermes as the Fourth Estate
entries.summary: Explains that the final integration debate is run with the Tribunal debate rules from Houses of Hermes: Societates, and that an argument bonus earned earlier from polemic texts can be applied to it.
quotes: it can be applied to any debate which encompasses aspects of the polemic philosophy

entries.title: Mundane Testimony at Tribunal
entries.requires: Saga arc: Order of Hermes as the Fourth Estate
entries.summary: Mundanes may attend Tribunal and give testimony in support of or against a case; mechanically this gives a small bonus to argument strength, with most of the value being roleplaying.
quotes: the testimony adds +1 to the argument strength

entries.title: Magical Displays Earn Reputation
entries.requires: Saga arc: Order of Hermes as the Fourth Estate
entries.summary: After a magus has published a polemic supporting integration, giving a community or noble a sufficiently powerful device or spell earns him experience in a Proponent Reputation.
quotes: earns the magus one experience point towards his Proponent of (ideal) Reputation

entries.title: Verditius: Verditius Magic
entries.requires: House Verditius: Initiation into Verditius Magic
entries.summary: Verditius magi craft the item during its first season of enchanting, add Verditius Runes (their Philosophiae) to Shape and Material bonuses, add their Craft Ability to Lab Totals, reduce the vis needed to open the item, and need casting tools for Formulaic and Ritual spells.
quotes: a magus who does so may add his score in the relevant Craft Ability to all Lab Totals for enchanting that item
the number of pawns of vis needed to open the item for enchantment is reduced by the magus's Craft score, to a minimum of one pawn

entries.title: Verditius Apprenticeship and Gauntlet
entries.summary: How a Verditius apprentice is initiated into the Outer Mystery while the Arts are opened, what the master must know to do it, and how the apprentice's Gauntlet is a masterpiece enchanted item made in an extra season.
quotes: Verditius magi must also have a score of 2 in Verditius Cult Lore.
The parens supplies the necessary vis, and gives the apprentice a season to work unaided in his laboratory.

entries.title: Forge-Companions and Venditores
entries.summary: Verditius ranks used in the Contest, plus the forge-companions who add to a magus's Lab Total when they share his Craft Ability and the venditores who sell his items to mundanes, and their murky legal status.
quotes: each forge-companion may add +1 per 5 levels of Craft Ability score he possesses to the maga's Lab Total.
A Verditius magus may have a number of forge-companions equal to his Leadership score.

entries.title: Verditius Vendettas
entries.summary: The non-lethal personal feuds between Verditius magi: how they start, what tactics are acceptable, the Reputation penalty for refusing one, and how the Primus ends escalating ones.
quotes: any magus who refuses a vendetta gains a bad Reputation of Dishonorable 4 in the House

entries.title: The Verditius Contest
entries.summary: The eighteen-year competition at Verdi in which Verditius magi enter their finest item in apprentice, journeyman and master categories; judging criteria, tie-breaking by the Primus and the order in which winners pick prizes.
quotes: The master category winner selects first, choosing three items for himself, the journeyman winner chooses two, followed by the apprentice winner who chooses a single item.

entries.title: Verditius Elder Runes
entries.requires: Initiation: Verditius Elder Runes (Verditius Minor Inner Mystery)
entries.summary: Elder runes (a table linking each rune to an Art and a tree) that can be inscribed on an item to double an Art for enchanting at the cost of a higher effect level and vis, with a bonus for matching wood and a higher seasonal vis limit.
quotes: Each rune adds five to the final level of effect of the power being instilled in the device
each inscribed rune allows the magus to double the Art that the rune represents, exactly like a magical focus
It costs a pawn of Art-specific vis to inscribe each elder rune.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.26 (Minor Breakthroughs)

entries.title: Becoming a Quaesitor
entries.summary: How a magus of any House is selected, mentored and appointed as a Quaesitor, and which Abilities the training and exposure covers in game terms.
quotes: In game terms this gives the candidate training and exposure to, Code of Hermes, Hermes Lore, Awareness, Folk Ken and Intrigue.

entries.title: Quaesitor in Good Standing
entries.summary: A Quaesitor needs a current signed letter from the Guernicus Primus to have authority to demand cooperation or preside at Tribunal.
quotes: This letter must be less than seven years old to be valid.

entries.title: Investigation Duties
entries.summary: A Quaesitor must investigate serious complaints but is entitled to seasons of his own each year, which may be accrued.
quotes: He is also entitled to at least three seasons every year to pursue his own studies or attend to covenant responsibilities.

entries.title: Investigation Immunity
entries.requires: Quaesitor (or an agent) in a justified investigation
entries.summary: Limits on when a Quaesitor may use Intellego magic in investigations without breaching the scrying prohibition, what liability remains for incidental discoveries, and who else the immunity covers.
quotes: However, Intellego Mentem magic can never be used on magi or their servants without their permission.

related.text: Scrying on Members of the Order

entries.title: Sanctum Invasions
entries.summary: A Quaesitor may enter a sanctum under investigation, during which time they are under forfeit immunity, though investigation immunity protects them from charges about the invasion.
